use verbose.  The reason why it looks like it is "done", is because

"done", but that is tricky to automate).

> ...
> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chipType)
> lapply(cs, print)

and see if you get an error already there?  If you do, then we're on
the right track.  If so, select the/an array that gives you an error,
say the first one, and do:

> cf <- getFile(cs, 1)
> print(cf)

I have just updated R to R.2.5 and bioconductor (2.0) on my linux
(Ubuntu), so far, so good.
I then installed aroma following the installation guidelines above.
This was fine until:

Loading required package: digest

installation of package 'aroma.affymetrix' had non-zero exit status

library(aroma.affymetrix)

aroma.affymetrix v0.4.3 (2007-03-15) successfully loaded. See ?
aroma.affymetrix for help.

address (nil), cause 'memory not mapped'

 1: .Call("digest", as.character(object), as.integer(algoint),
as.integer(length),     PACKAGE = "digest")

paste("Error in", dcall, ": ")        LONGCALL <- 30        if

invisible(structure(msg, class = "try-error"))})

Possible actions:

4: exit R saving workspace

Any ideas?
cheers

Lavinia.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

ok.  It fails to get a valid CEL header timestamp.  I'll robustify the
code so it detects that and returns NA instead.

MORE TROUBLESHOOTING:

Could you report what you get when you do:

> getHeader(cf)

It will be a bit of output, but that will help me locate the problem.
To be sure the email clients does not mess with the output, could you
please also attach the 'celHeader.txt' file generated by the
following:

> sink("celHeader.txt"); print(getHeader(cf)); sink()

This will allow me to locate the problem and return a valid CEL header
timestamp.

PATCH:

Then, download the patch I've made available, by:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
> downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")
> quit()

...and restart R and retry:

> library(aroma.affymetrix)
...
Patching patches/aroma.affymetrix/20070510/AffymetrixCelFile.calibrateAllelicCro
sstalk.R
Patching patches/aroma.affymetrix/20070510/AffymetrixCelFile.R
Patching patches/aroma.affymetrix/20070510/ExonRmaPlm.R
>

Now, see what the following give:

> getTimestamp(cf)
> print(cf)

It should report 'NA' as the timestamp.

/Henrik

best of my understanding this happens when you load an R v2.4.x build

per se.  You can reproduce the error with:

> library(R.utils)
> parse(text="")

R.utils and try again.  The above two lines should now return

With this fix, the rest of the installation of aroma.affymetrix should
work again.

messages.subject: Re: Problems with the new Calvin CEL file format (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: zero-length argument error)
messages.subject_clean: Problems with the new Calvin CEL file format (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: zero-length argument error)
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

Ok. First, good that the patch for timestamp works. I will soon
release a new version of aroma.affymetrix etc. solving recent problems
and problems with R v2.5.0.

Second, the CEL files seems to be in the new/upcoming binary file
format called "Calvin".  This is probably why the timestamp is lost -
I have to look into the details if there is a timestamp in this new
file format.

Third, I have not done any analysis with aroma.affymetrix on this new
file format.  However, it should support *read* data from Calvin
files, but it does *not* support writing/updating Calvin files, and
that is where the problem is.  Your error message occurs when
aroma.affymetrix first copies a (Calvin) CEL files and then tries to
update it (which is only supported for standard binary (XDR) CEL
files).

I do not see that the package will support writing Calvin CEL files
anytime soon.  A workaround for you is to convert all Calvin CEL files
in regular binary CEL files using convertCel() available in
affxparser.  You only have to do this ones for you raw data.  I
haven't tried converting Calvin CEL files, but only ASCII CEL files.
However, I don't think you should have any problems.

Could you please point me to an Affymetrix URL where I can download
these Calvin CEL files?  The first solution for aroma.affymetrix is
probably to detect Calvin file formats, and instead of copying them
(as tried below), using convertCel().  That should be fairly
transparent to the user, except that it takes extra time.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problems with the new Calvin CEL file format (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: zero-length argument error)
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problems with the new Calvin CEL file format (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: zero-length argument error)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

yes, it could be related to the fact that the 'header' field of the
Calvin CEL header is empty.  Try to use convertCel(..., verbose=TRUE).
 However, the solution/patch for that will be different, since this is
unrelated to aroma.affymetrix.  I'll look into the problem when I have
time.  See if you can find any CEL converters on the Affymetrix
website, e.g. the 'apt-cel-transformer' tool part of the Affymetrix
Power Tools [http://www.affymetrix.com/support/developer/tools/devnettools.affx]
might be able to do a "one-to-one transformation" of a CEL file...
maybe.

/Henrik

On 5/10/07, Mark Robinson <mark.rob...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > f<-dir("rawData/tissues/HuGene-1_0-st-v1/","CEL",full=T)
> > for(i in seq(along=f)) {
> + nfn<-sub("WTGene1","WTGene1_XDA",f[i])
> + convertCel(f[i],nfn)
> + }
> Error in sprintf(fmt, ...) : zero-length argument
> In addition: Warning message:
> Coercing LHS to a list
>
> Does the same thing need to  be applied to the convertCel function?
>
> Thanks,
> Mark
>
>
>
> On 5/11/07, Henrik Bengtsson <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
> >
> > Hi.
> >
> > Ok. First, good that the patch for timestamp works. I will soon
> > release a new version of aroma.affymetrix etc. solving recent problems
> > and problems with R v2.5.0.
> >
> > Second, the CEL files seems to be in the new/upcoming binary file
> > format called "Calvin".  This is probably why the timestamp is lost -
> > I have to look into the details if there is a timestamp in this new
> > file format.
> >
> > Third, I have not done any analysis with aroma.affymetrix on this new
> > file format.  However, it should support *read* data from Calvin
> > files, but it does *not* support writing/updating Calvin files, and
> > that is where the problem is.  Your error message occurs when
> > aroma.affymetrix first copies a (Calvin) CEL files and then tries to
> > update it (which is only supported for standard binary (XDR) CEL
> > files).
> >
> > I do not see that the package will support writing Calvin CEL files
> > anytime soon.  A workaround for you is to convert all Calvin CEL files
> > in regular binary CEL files using convertCel() available in
> > affxparser.  You only have to do this ones for you raw data.  I
> > haven't tried converting Calvin CEL files, but only ASCII CEL files.
> > However, I don't think you should have any problems.
> >
> > Could you please point me to an Affymetrix URL where I can download
> > these Calvin CEL files?  The first solution for aroma.affymetrix is
> > probably to detect Calvin file formats, and instead of copying them
> > (as tried below), using convertCel().  That should be fairly
> > transparent to the user, except that it takes extra time.
> >
> > Cheers
> >
> > Henrik

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.5.0 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

aroma.affymetrix v0.5.0 is now available together with many updated
R.* packages.  Here are some comments on the update:

GENERAL:

o From now on, aroma.affymetrix will be developed with R v2.5.x. This
release is the last release that will be verified against with R
v2.4.x.
o Package passes R CMD check on Rv2.5.0 (and R v2.4.1).
o Package pass redundancy tests on R v2.5.0 (and R v2.4.1) on both
Windows XP and Linux.

NEWS / UPDATES:

o Added default zoom levels to updateSamplesFile() for
ChromosomeExplorer. This is applies the first time process() is
called.
o Removed dependency of the R.image package by removing writeSpatial()
for the AffymetrixCelFile class.  Use writeImage() instead.
o Now patchPackage(..., deleteOld=TRUE) removes not only old patches,
but also patches that are older than the package itself.  Thus, when
loading the package, all old patches are automatically removed.
o Added argument 'apply=TRUE' to downloadPackagePatch() so that
downloaded patches are applied immediately after being downloaded.

BUG FIXES:

o getProbeAffinityFile() of ExonRmaPlm did not return the correct subclass.
o calibrateAllelicCrosstalk() for AffymetrixCelFile would output
filenames containing only the name but not the tags.
o If no valid timestamp was identified in the CEL header by
getTimestamp() of AffymetrixCelFile, then as.character() would give
"Error in sprintf(fmt, ...) : zero-length argument".  Now it returns
NA instead as a fallback if no valid timestamp is found.
o getRegions() and getLog2Ratios() of GladModel would give an error if
only a subset of the chromosomes where queried.

See group page for instructions how to update.  Any patches downloaded
previously will automatically be deleted.

/Henrik

There are actually links to the both types of CEL files from that link
(http://www.affymetrix.com/support/technical/sample_data/
hugene_1_0_array_data.affx) ... the AGCC (Calvin) and the GCOS (XDA).

Had I read Elizabeth's post (http://groups.google.com.au/group/aroma-

thoroughly, I would've known not to use the AGCC type at this stage.

Cheers,
Mark

messages.body_plain:
Following these guidelines:

At 08:40 PM 20/05/2007 -0700, Henrik Bengtsson wrote:

Now the example from cfit.matrix works!
> example(cfit.matrix)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
- - - - -
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Simulate data
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
- - - - -
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> N <- 1000

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Simulate genotypes
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> g <- sample(c("AA", "AB",
"AB", "BB"), size=N, replace=TRUE)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Simulate concentrations of allele A and allele B
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> X <- matrix(rexp(N), nrow=N, ncol=2)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> colnames(X) <- c("A", "B")

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> X[g == "AA", "B"] <- 0

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> X[g == "BB", "A"] <- 0

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> X[g == "AB",] <- X[g == "AB",] /
2

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Transform noisy X
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> xi <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05), ncol=2)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> a0 <- c(0,0)+0.3

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> A <- matrix(c(0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 0.8), nrow=2,
byrow=TRUE)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> A <- apply(A, MARGIN=2, FUN=function(u) u /
sqrt(sum(u^2)))

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> Z <- t(a0 + A %*% t(X + xi))

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Add noise to Y
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> eps <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05),
ncol=2)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> Y <- Z + eps

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> layout(matrix(1:4, ncol=2, byrow=TRUE))

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> xlab <- "Allele A"

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> ylab <- "Allele B"

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> lim <- c(0,6)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> plot(X, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> points(Z, col="blue")

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> points(Y, col="red")

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> legend("topright", pch=19, pt.cex=2,
legend=c("X", "Z", "Y"),
col=c("black", "blue", "red"),
title="Variables:", bg="#eeeeee")

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
- - - - -
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Fit model
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
- - - - -
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> alpha <- c(0.10, 0.075, 0.05, 0.03, 0.01, 0.001)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> fit <- cfit(Y, dump=2, alpha=alpha, q=2, Q=98)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> Ms <- fit$M

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> col <- terrain.colors(length(Ms))

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> #col <- rainbow(length(Ms))
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> col[length(Ms)] <- "red"

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> lim <- c(-0.5,5)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> plot(Y, cex=0.8, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim,
main="Y")

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> for (kk in seq(along=Ms)) {
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>+   M <- Ms[[kk]]
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>+   points(M, pch=19, cex=2.5, col=col[kk])
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>+   lines(M, col=col[kk], lwd=2)
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>+   text(M, cex=0.8, labels=kk)
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>+ }

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> legend("topright", pch=19, pt.cex=2, legend=c(alpha,
"final"), col=col, title=expression(alpha),
bg="#eeeeee")

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> apex <- which.min(apply(M, MARGIN=1, FUN=function(u)
sum(u^2)))

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> a0hat <- M[apex,]

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> Ahat <- M[-apex,]

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> Ahat <- apply(Ahat, MARGIN=2, FUN=function(u) u /
sqrt(sum(u^2)))

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> if (sum(Ahat[c(1,4)]^2) < sum(Ahat[c(2,3)]^2)) {
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>+   Ahat <- matrix(Ahat[c(2,1,4,3)], nrow=2)
cft.mt <http://cft.mt>+ }

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> Ainv <- solve(Ahat)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> Xhat <- t(Ainv %*% (t(Y) - a0hat))

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> cat("True A:\n")
True A:

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> print(A)

[,1]      [,2]
[1,] 0.9938837 0.1240347
[2,] 0.1104315 0.9922779

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> cat("Estimated A:\n")
Estimated A:

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> print(Ahat)

V1        V2
[1,] 0.9873211 0.1216088
[2,] 0.1587355 0.9925781

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> plot(Xhat, cex=0.8, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim,
main=expression(hat(X)))

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> x1 <- par("usr")[2]

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> y1 <- par("usr")[4]

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> lines(x=c(0,x1), y=c(0,0), col="red",
lwd=2)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> lines(x=c(0,0), y=c(0,y1), col="red",
lwd=2)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> lines(x=c(0,x1), y=c(0,y1), col="blue",
lwd=2)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> plot(X[,1], Xhat[,1], cex=0.8, xlab=expression(X),
ylab=expression(hat(X)), xlim=lim, ylim=lim)

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> points(X[,2], Xhat[,2], cex=0.8,
col="red")

cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> abline(a=0, b=1, lwd=2)
>

allelic crosstalk calibration now works without any warnings or
errors.

cheers

Lavinia

Hi all.

Since the upgrade to R 2.5, I cannot get affxparser to compile on the
mac.  Any suggestions?  Is there something that has changed (or needs
to change with it)?

Below is the installation outp

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] mac compile error - affxparser
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

Kasper is the one that might help out.  He only reads the
aroma.affymetrix list once in a while, so I would suggest that you
send this to the Bioconductor list instead.  There, he and others will
be able to help you faster.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: Problem with the sfit package
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've just committed a new version of the sfit package that fixes the
problem below that might occur on some Unix systems.  Just do:

source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R")
hbLite("aroma.affymetrix")

and that should update all packages including sfit.

Cheers

Henrik

On 5/20/07, Lavinia Gordon <lavinia...@mcri.edu.au> wrote:

>  Following these guidelines:
>
>  At 08:40 PM 20/05/2007 -0700, Henrik Bengtsson wrote:
>
> library(sfit)
> source("http://www.braju.com/R/patches/sfit/20070520/fix.R")
>  print(getOption("cfit"))
>  readLines(pipe(getOption("cfit")))
>  > library(sfit)
>  Loading required package: R.oo
>  R.oo v1.2.7 (2006-04-07) successfully loaded. See ?R.oo for help.
>  sfit v0.1.1 (2006-05-20) successfully loaded. See ?sfit for help.
>  >
> source("http://www.braju.com/R/patches/sfit/20070520/fix.R")
>  Warning message:
>  Method already existed and was overwritten: cfit.matrix in:
> setMethodS3.default("cfit", "matrix", function(y, k = ncol(y) +
>  > print(getOption("cfit"))
>  [1] "\"/usr/local/lib/R/library/sfit/bin/cfit\""
>  > readLines(pipe(getOption("cfit")))
>
>  cfit [ options ] k [ data [ weight ]]
>
>  Fit a simplex with k vertices to points in the file <data> (stdin
>  is used if not supplied).
>
>  <weight> is a file of point weights (if not supplied, w_j = 1/n).
>
>  -h, --help      this help
>  -v, --verbose   dump progress to stderr
>
>  -i, --Minit <filename>    initial simplex
>  -d, --dump <int>          dump mode (0 none, 1 final, 2 each alpha, 3 each
> REX)
>  -M, --outM <filename>     where M is dumped [ stdout ]
>  -X, --outX <filename>     where X is dumped
>
>  -a, --alpha <num,num,...> comma- or space-separated sequence of alpha
>  -T, --maxiter <int>       maximum number of REX steps
>  -f, --frobratio <num>     ratio of ||DM||/||M|| (inner loop convergence)
>      --QRtolerance <num>   ratio of ||q_i||/||q_1|| (QR termination)
>
>  -C, --constraints  <int>  0 none, 1 nonnegative, 2 box, 3 probability-like
>  -x, --lubox <lb,ub>       lower and upper bound in box constraints
>                            (specifying this turns on --constraints 2). If
> this
>                            is not specified, the dimension-specific lower
> and
>                            upper bounds are read from a file `lubox'
> containing
>                            2 x m  matrix of lower- and upper-bound vectors.
>
>  -o, --origin <filename>   origin vector, offset data by this vector
> [default 0]
>  -g, --gamma <num>        `eye-height' in projective transform [default 0]
>  -u, --viewdir <filename> `viewing direction' vector [ meanY/(meanY^T meanY)
> ]
>      --u_1T                u = (1,1,1,... )
>  -D, --denom_weight        use the denominators as observation weights
>      --outPY <filename>    save the transformed Y into this file
>      --outPM <filename>    dump projective-transformed M (according
>                            to the dump mode option).
>
>  -q, --chopless <num>      assign zero weight to points if u^T y is less
>  -Q, --chopmore <num>      or more than the specified percentiles.
>
>  -R, --robust <num>        robust coefficient (if compiled with
> -DWITH_ROBUST)
>  character(0)
>  >
>
>  Now the example from cfit.matrix works!
>  > example(cfit.matrix)
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
> - -
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Simulate data
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
> - -
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> N <- 1000
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Simulate genotypes
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> g <- sample(c("AA", "AB", "AB", "BB"), size=N, replace=TRUE)
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Simulate concentrations of allele A and allele B
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> X <- matrix(rexp(N), nrow=N, ncol=2)
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> colnames(X) <- c("A", "B")
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> X[g == "AA", "B"] <- 0
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> X[g == "BB", "A"] <- 0
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> X[g == "AB",] <- X[g == "AB",] / 2
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Transform noisy X
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> xi <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05), ncol=2)
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> a0 <- c(0,0)+0.3
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> A <- matrix(c(0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 0.8), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> A <- apply(A, MARGIN=2, FUN=function(u) u / sqrt(sum(u^2)))
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> Z <- t(a0 + A %*% t(X + xi))
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Add noise to Y
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> eps <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05), ncol=2)
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> Y <- Z + eps
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> layout(matrix(1:4, ncol=2, byrow=TRUE))
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> xlab <- "Allele A"
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> ylab <- "Allele B"
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> lim <- c(0,6)
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> plot(X, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim)
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> points(Z, col="blue")
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> points(Y, col="red")
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> legend("topright", pch=19, pt.cex=2, legend=c("X", "Z", "Y"),
> col=c("black", "blue", "red"), title="Variables:", bg="#eeeeee")
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
> - -
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # Fit model
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
> - -
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> alpha <- c(0.10, 0.075, 0.05, 0.03, 0.01, 0.001)
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> fit <- cfit(Y, dump=2, alpha=alpha, q=2, Q=98)
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> Ms <- fit$M
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> col <- terrain.colors(length(Ms))
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> #col <- rainbow(length(Ms))
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> col[length(Ms)] <- "red"
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> lim <- c(-0.5,5)
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> plot(Y, cex=0.8, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim,
> main="Y")
>
>  cft.mt <http://cft.mt>> for (kk in seq(along=Ms)) {

messages.subject: Software QA: Requests for redundancy tests
messages.subject_clean: Software QA: Requests for redundancy tests
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

In order to assure correctness between updates and minimizing the risk
for new bugs when fixing others, so called redundancy tests are
needed.  Right now I have a few test scripts running on public data
that I use for this, but these are only for copy-number analysis and
they are far for complete.  So I am asking for you help to create more
test scripts for other cases, e.g. exon array analysis and gene
expression analysis.

I am looking for scripts that allows you to test various
algorithms/code using *public* data. So, please forward your test
scripts and instructions on what public data you use and ideally where
to download it.  One criteria is that any user should be able to run
the tests.  Try to base it on as few number of arrays as possible in
order to keep the processing time to a minimum.  I've create a page:

 Pages / For Developers / Redundancy Tests
 [ http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/edit/redundancy-tests-2 ]

with existing redundancy tests to give you an idea what is needed.

Any member should be able to update this page, so please feel free to
add test sets yourself and then I download them and use them.  When
you click "Save & Publish" your editing will be available to all.  You
will then get to a page where you can also "Post message" to the
mailing list about your update; do NOT do that but send a separate
message to the mailing list instead.  [If you have problems editing,
send the text to me and I'll add it.]

With a good set of redundancy tests the quality of the package will
increase so we all can focus more on the science and less on software
problems.

Thanks

Henrik

messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Software QA: Requests for redundancy tests
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

test scripts that I am looking for are regular R scripts that can be
called using source() and  that uses aroma.affymetrix classes and
methods to analysis Affymetrix data.

The script could be as simple as defining an AffymetrixCelSet and
calling some its methods (e.g. getName() or just print()), but most
likely it is defining a CEL set, runs some normalization,
summarization etc.  A test script is expected to run to the end
without errors.  This will assert that the aroma.affymetrix code does
not have immediate bugs.

On top of this the script could add tests for numerical results, e.g.
if one have found that the log-ratio for a certain gene is in
[0.51,0.52] by using aroma.affymetrix v0.5.0, and we trust that, we
can add a stopifnot() statement to assert this; if new code, in
aroma.affymetrix or in dependent BioC packages, introduce big changes,
that might give in different numerical results and the test script
will detect that.

See the test scripts I've put on the group page for examples. [ Until
the group pages go public, you will need a Google account (you have
one if you have a gmail account - it is easy to get one) to access the
pages.  Send me your Google account and I'll add it to the members
list. ]

So, the purpose of the redundancy testing is to detect (and locate)
surprising results as early as possible.  The more test scripts we
have the more of the underlying code is evaluated and the more bugs we
fill identify (there are always bugs left in any code!).

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: mac compile error - affxparser

Hi Mark

You may or may not be aware that the compiler suite etc changed from
R-2.4.x to R-2.5.0. You need Xcode 2.4.1 (from Apples website) and you
need to make sure you are using GCC 4 by doing a
# gcc_select
at the command line (you can use gcc_select to change compiler from
version 3 to 4).

You also need the fortran compiler fra CRAN - when you install the dmg
image of R from CRAN you need to click "customize" and choose the
fortran compiler.

If you need to clean out your old installation (recommended) you can
do it by
# sudo rm -R /usr/local/gcc4.0

Kasper

messages.body_snippet:
Hi Mark

You may or may not be aware that the compiler suite etc changed from
R-2.4.x to R-2.5.0. You need Xcode 2.4.1 (from Apples website) and you
need to make sure you are using GCC 4 by doing a
#

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: mac compile error - affxparser
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kasper.

I have Xcode 2.4.1 installed and it appears to be using gcc 4.

----
mac1187:~ mrobinson$ gcc_select
Current default compiler:
gcc version 4.0.1 (Apple Computer, Inc. build 5367)
----
mac1187:~ mrobinson$ gcc  -v
Using built-in specs.
Target: powerpc-apple-darwin8
Configured with: /private/var/tmp/gcc/gcc-5367.obj~1/src/configure --
disable-checking -enable-werror --prefix=/usr --mandir=/share/man --
enable-languages=c,objc,c++,obj-c++ --program-transform-name=/^[cg]
[^.-]*$/s/$/-4.0/ --with-gxx-include-dir=/include/c++/4.0.0 --with-
slibdir=/usr/lib --build=powerpc-apple-darwin8 --host=powerpc-apple-
darwin8 --target=powerpc-apple-darwin8
Thread model: posix
gcc version 4.0.1 (Apple Computer, Inc. build 5367)
----

Will enquire about the fortran compiler.

Mark

On 23/05/2007, at 4:05 PM, Kasper Daniel Hansen wrote:

>
> Hi Mark
>
> You may or may not be aware that the compiler suite etc changed from
> R-2.4.x to R-2.5.0. You need Xcode 2.4.1 (from Apples website) and you
> need to make sure you are using GCC 4 by doing a
> # gcc_select
> at the command line (you can use gcc_select to change compiler from
> version 3 to 4).
>
> You also need the fortran compiler fra CRAN - when you install the dmg
> image of R from CRAN you need to click "customize" and choose the
> fortran compiler.
>
> If you need to clean out your old installation (recommended) you can
> do it by
> # sudo rm -R /usr/local/gcc4.0
>
> Kasper

messages.subject: FYI: Affymetrix released Genome-Wide Human SNP Array 6.0
messages.subject_clean: FYI: Affymetrix released Genome-Wide Human SNP Array 6.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

for your information, Affymetrix just released Genome-Wide Human SNP
Array 6.0, which interrogates 1.8 million loci, with about 900K SNPs
and about 900 non-polymorphic copy-number probes.  The Affymetrix
press release is here:

  http://tinyurl.com/yqaual

The main impression is that this will be a much better chip than the
5.0 chip, which seems to have been quite an intermediate chip type.
I've added a page for this chip type on the aroma.affymetrix group
page, and will add more information there as soon as I get it.  When I
start working with this chip type myself, I will design and upload
necessary annotation files for doing fragment-length normalization and
copy-number analysis.

If you plan to work with chip type, think about your reference set.
It is clear that using a pool of in-house (=same microarray facility)
references hybridization, compared to using say public HapMap hybs,
improves the signal-to-noise ratio substantially.  It is ok to use
anonymous samples (even those with CN aberrations).  So, if possible,
try to run as many hybridizations as possible early on.  For the 500K
chip set we found that we got stronger signals as we increase the pool
of reference samples to 20-30 hybs and it will most likely improve
beyond that.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On 5/24/07, mbchip <mbc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi all,
>
>  I am new to aroma.affymetrix  and have a couple of questions
>  to get started.  I want to use the  sample data sets for copy
>  number analysis on Affy's web site: 500K: 9 Tumor/Normal Pairs
>  derived from human cancer cell lines and X Chromosome titration set (3X,
> 4X, and 5X).
>  How to convert those .DTT files to CEL files?  Also, where  can I get the
> CDF file
>  for SNP 500K array?

To get started with a copy-number analysis, I recommend you start with
a small number of HapMap 500K arrays and only for one of the two
available chip types, e.g. Mapping250K_Nsp.  Under "Pages", on the
aroma.affymetrix google group, I have created pages for some of the
common chip types.  For Mapping250K_Nsp you'll find links to public
data sets at the Affymetrix site, which in turn will link to the (270)
HapMap 500K samples.  These are easiest because for these you can
download CEL files one by one.   Affymetrix distribute the CDF files
in so called "library files" on their sites.

>
>  In addition, I want to try the example code cn500K.Rex.

Instead of that script, look at examples under Section "Use cases / Examples".

>  Where can I get those CEL and CDF files for the data
>  in this example 'SinclairA_etal_2006'?

The SinclairA_etal_2006 data set is private and not publicly available.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] same expression summaries as 'rma'
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

Yes, that overall banana curvature you show in your plot is due to the
fact that justRMA() do background correction but in your
aroma.affymetrix script you don't.  According to the help,
justRMA(..., background=TRUE, bgversion=2), does "use background
similar to pure R rma background given in affy version 1.1 and above".
 Note, the RmaPlm class does only do probe *summarization*, i.e.
log-additive modelling, but nothing else (on purpose).

I believe this is the background correction method that Ken
ported/implemented in the RmaBackgroundCorrection class of
aroma.affymetrix.  See also Section "Calibration and normalization of
probe-level data" in the group pages.

We have started a Section "Reproducibility of other implementations"
for the purpose of showing that aroma.affymetrix can reproduce
existing methods.  It would be great if you could add a subsection to
that page with some figures showing how well you manage to reproduce
justRMA() - code snippets would be even better.

Let us know how it goes!

Cheers

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
OK, much closer.  Should I expect better correspondence than this:
http://bioinf.wehi.edu.au/folders/mrobinson/aroma/rma.vs.RmaPlm1.png

Here is my code so far ... will add this snippet and a couple other
tests once I've figure this all out.  Will add a few more tests:
RMA, gcRMA, ?

Mark

----------
getExprs<-function(chp) {
   cn<-getNames(chp)
   ru<-readUnits(chp)
   rn<-names(ru)
   d<-log2(t(matrix(unlist(ru),nrow=length(cn))))
   rownames(d)<-rn
   colnames(d)<-cn
   d
}
library(aroma.affymetrix)

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8); timestampOn(verbose)
name <- "tissues"
chip1<- "HG-U133_Plus_2"
chip2<- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
chip3<- "HuGene-1_0-st-v1"
cs1 <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chip1)
bc1 <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs1)
csBC1 <- process(bc1)
qn1 <- QuantileNormalization(csBC1, typesToUpdate="pm")

csN1 <- process(qn1, verbose=verbose) #time required
plm1.merge <- RmaPlm(csN1)
fit(plm1.merge, verbose=verbose) #time required
chp1.merge<-getChipEffectSet(plm1.merge)

d1<-getExprs(chp1.merge)

fn.u133<-dir("rawData/tissues/HG-U133_Plus_2/","CEL",full=T)

u133.rma<-justRMA(filenames=fn.u133,celfile.path=".")
d<-exprs(u133.rma)

m<-match(rownames(d),rownames(d1))

png("rma.vs.RmaPlm1.png")
plot(d[,1],d1[m,1],pch=19,xlab="justRMA-
affy",ylab="RmaBackgroundCorrection+RmaPlm-aroma.affymetrix")
abline(0,1,col="blue")
dev.off()
----------

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark.

Yes, that made a difference.  I am not familiar with the details of
justRMA() and what could cause the observed different, which now seems
to be mostly "random" errors.  One difference I am quite sure about is
that QuantileNormalization() is calculating the target distribution
using non-robust mean instead of median, but I doubt that would cause
such a large difference.

BTW, have you made sure the order of the arrays are the same in
aroma.affymetrix and justRMA()?  I think this should be the case, but
you never know.

I would like to suggest to try to track down the sources of
differences.  Looking at justRMA() we have the following arguments to
play with:

 justRMA(..., normalize=TRUE, background=TRUE, bgversion=2)

Arguments 'rm.mask', 'rm.outliers', 'rm.extra' can be ignored as long
as they are FALSE as aroma.affymetrix is not doing any of that.

Try to reproduce results in this order:

1) justRMA(..., normalize=FALSE, background=FALSE)
2) justRMA(..., normalize=TRUE, background=FALSE)
3) justRMA(..., normalize=TRUE, background=TRUE, bgversion=2)

Some comments on your code:

The following getExprs() is probably faster:

getExprs <- function(ces, ...) {
  cdf <- getCdf(ces);
  theta <- extractMatrix(ces, ..., returnUgcMap=TRUE);
  ugcMap <- attr(theta, "unitGroupCellMap");
  rownames(theta) <- getUnitNames(cdf, ugcMap[,"unit"]);
  log2(theta);
}

You can replace
fn.u133<-dir("rawData/tissues/HG-U133_Plus_2/","CEL",full=T) with

  fn.u133 <- getPathnames(cs1)

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: Wish: User's wish list
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

it's now been more than three months since beta testing of
aroma.affymetrix first started.  Since then more than 10 new version
have been released and the package is getting more and more stable.
Now I wish to ask you for your feedback on how the package can be
improved or what features you wish to be added.  This could be
anything from missing methods to reports you would to generate, or
comments on things that are confusing or could be improved.  Please
send you thoughts to the mailing list ***with prefix "Wish:" in the
subject line***.  Brain storming is ok, but it is better if you even
could specify exact method interfaces.  Try to be as precise as
possible.

Example: I would to see an implementation of affy::justRMA() in
aroma.affymetrix that as close as possible imitates the results of
affy:

  yetAnotherJustRma(celSet, rm.mask=FALSE, rm.outliers=FALSE,
rm.extra=FALSE, normalize=TRUE,  background=TRUE, bgversion=2)

Blah blah...

Example: Add an option to specify a ProbeAffinityFile when fitting a
ProbeLevelModel.  This way one do not have to refit the model each
time, e.g. you fit 30 arrays and then get another array to be
included.  One option is to add an argument to fit(..., paf=paf) or a
new method, say, setProbeAffinityFile(<plm>, paf).  Blah blah ...

I will then try to collect all in a Section "User's wish list" on the
group page.  Disclaimer: I cannot promise to implement all, but it
will give me/us a good feeling what is missing and what can be
improved, and how to prioritize.  And of course, if you have more or
less general scripts or methods that you think would fit in the
package, and be useful to others, I'm happy to include such.

Cheers

Henrik
